**The 56 Signers of the United States Declaration of Independence**

The Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Continental Congress on **July 4, 1776**, but the formal signing ceremony took place on **August 2, 1776** at the Pennsylvania State House (now Independence Hall) in Philadelphia. All 56 delegates who had voted for independence signed the document. They came from the thirteen colonies and represented a wide range of professions, ages, and political views.

| # | Name | Colony / State | Notable Roles |
|---|------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | **John Hancock** | Massachusetts | President of the Continental Congress; famously large signature |
| 2 | **Samuel Adams** | Massachusetts | Revolutionary leader, “Father of the American Revolution” |
| 3 | **John Adams** | Massachusetts | Future Vice‑President and President |
| 4 | **Robert Treat Paine** | Massachusetts | Lawyer, former governor of the colony |
| 5 | **Joseph Hewes** | North Carolina | Merchant, former U.S. Representative |
| 6 | **William Hooper** | North Carolina | Lawyer, former governor |
| 7 | **John Penn** | North Carolina | Former governor |

| 9 | **Thomas Jefferson** | Virginia | Principal author of the Declaration |

|11 | **George Mason** | Virginia | Author of the Virginia Declaration of Rights |
|12 | **Richard Henry Lee** | Virginia | Proposed the resolution for independence |

**Key Points**

- **Total signers:** 56 delegates.
- **Signatures were added on August 2, 1776** (though the Declaration was adopted on July 4).
- **Signers represented all thirteen colonies.**
- **Notable figures:** Thomas Jefferson (principal author), John Hancock (largest signature), George Washington (military commander), Benjamin Franklin (statesman), James Madison (future Constitution drafter), and many others who played crucial roles in the Revolution.
